gizmo.title: Concept quest game
gizmo.description: An overworld to wander. Concepts find you and ask a question. Answer right to defeat one and unlock its house. The recap shows tries and what to review.

configure.title: Quest
configure.description: The prompt shown on the start screen. Tell the player what the journey is for.

configure.title: Concepts
configure.description: Each concept is a house with a monster.

properties.title: Short phrase shown after it is unlocked
What it is
properties.description: Shown when the house unlocks and in the review list.

properties.title: Question
properties.description: Asked when the concept finds you. Leave empty to ask which description belongs to it.

properties.title: Choices, one per line
properties.description: Put the RIGHT answer on the first line. The game shuffles them.

configure.title: Center label
configure.description: The idea all of the concepts add up to.

configure.title: After the game
configure.description: Optional. Replaces the copy-a-prompt box on the finish panel with your own content, such as a next step or a link.

configure.title: Extra buttons after the game
configure.description: Optional. Buttons or links shown beside Play again on the finish panel.

advanced.title: Hearts
advanced.description: Wrong answers before the concept gets away.

advanced.title: Character seed
advanced.description: Any text. The same seed always makes the same character. This is the same seed the HAX avatar uses.

advanced.title: Use the signed in person's character
advanced.description: When someone is signed in to HAX, the character looks like their own avatar. Everyone else sees the seed above.

advanced.title: Line above the prompt
advanced.description: Leave empty for the default line.

advanced.title: Prompt to copy
advanced.description: Shown on the finish panel with a copy button. Clear it to hide the box.

advanced.title: Game name
advanced.description: Names this game in progress events and OER Schema markup.

advanced.title: Game id
advanced.description: Optional. Tells this game apart from others on the page in progress events.

nodes.label: Accessible
nodes.text: HAX will always strive to maximize accessibility. The best time to make content accessible is the moment it is created, so HAX builds that into authoring instead of leaving it for later.
nodes.question: When is the best time to make content accessible?
nodes.choices:
The moment it is created
Right before it is published
After someone complains
Only for public sites

nodes.label: Extensible
nodes.text: Nothing in HAX is monolithic. The ecosystem keeps growing and contributions are welcome, so the system can be extended sustainably.
nodes.question: What does it mean that HAX is non-monolithic?
nodes.choices:
It keeps growing as people add to it
It ships as one big package
Only the core team can change it
It cannot be extended

nodes.label: Free and Open
nodes.text: Open documentation, open APIs and an open community. Content moves freely into and out of HAX, everything generates static files, and it costs nothing to use.
nodes.question: What happens to your content if you leave HAX?
nodes.choices:
It moves out freely as static files
It stays locked inside HAX
It is deleted
You pay to export it

nodes.label: Efficient
nodes.text: Built to perform well through good methodology, low-level browser APIs, micro-services and lazy loading.
nodes.question: Which of these helps HAX stay efficient?
nodes.choices:
Lazy loading elements only when they are needed
Loading every element on every page
Shipping a heavy framework
Rebuilding the page on every click
nodes.hint: Load only what the page uses.

nodes.label: Platform Agnostic
nodes.text: HAX output works on its own, inside HAXcms or HAXiam, or on plain static pages, with no hosting-specific backend to depend on.
nodes.question: Where can HAX content run?
nodes.choices:
Standalone, in HAXcms or HAXiam, or on plain static pages
Only inside one vendor's hosting
Only with one specific database
Only on a single campus network

nodes.label: Remixable
nodes.text: Duplicate a site, switch themes on the fly and reshape the structure of a whole site or a single page. The platform and what it produces are meant to be remixed.
nodes.question: Which of these can you do to remix a HAX site?
nodes.choices:
Duplicate it and switch themes on the fly
Nothing, sites are fixed once made
Edit it only through a vendor
Change the theme only by rewriting every page
nodes.hint: Themes can change on the fly.

nodes.label: Sustainable
nodes.text: Sustainable for the planet, with less data and battery use, and for the long run, because an open source community can outlive any single vendor.
nodes.question: Why is HAX sustainable beyond using less energy?
nodes.choices:
An open source community can outlive any single vendor
It needs a yearly subscription
It depends on one company
It is rebuilt from scratch every year

properties.finishText: Every concept has been defeated and every house is open.
properties.quest: Wander the overworld. When a concept finds you, answer its question to defeat it and unlock its house.
properties.finishLead: Paste this into Claude to keep practicing.
